<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par163 />{{GHGmargin-letter|163|d}}
Rem. The principal statement, to which {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}} appends an exception, must sometimes be supplied from the context; thus, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=14}} (I desire nothing else) ''except that thou remember me'', equivalent to ''only do thou remember'', &c. (cf. 106 n, note 2; but it is probably better to read {{GHGheb|text=אַךְ}} for {{GHGheb|text=כִּי}}). Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=6|verse=8}}, where {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}}, equivalent to ''nothing but'', is used before an infinitive, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=8}}, equivalent to ''only'', before a noun. Similarly when {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}} after an oath introduces an emphatic assurance, e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=20}} ''as the Lord liveth'' (I can do nothing else) ''except I run after him'', &c.; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=21}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=12}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, and even without the oath, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=7}}; cf. the Rem. on ''c''.<section end=par163 />

<section begin=par164 />{{GHGpar-heading|164|Temporal Clauses}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|164|a}}
'''1.''' The relations of time existing between two different actions or events are frequently expressed without the aid of a conjunction simply by juxtaposition:—

(''a'') Actions or events are represented as wholly or in part ''simultaneous'' by connecting a noun-clause with another noun-clause or verbal-clause introduced by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} (or {{GHGheb|text=וְהִנֵּה}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=6}} ''and Noah'' was ''six hundred years old'' (prop. ''a son of six hundred years''), {{GHGheb|text=וְהַמַּבּוּל הָיָה}} and (i.e. ''when'') ''the flood was''. This is especially the case when the predicate of the noun-clause (frequently introduced by {{GHGheb|text=עוֹד|translate=still}}) is expressed by an active participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=16}} f. {{GHGheb|text=עוֹד זֶה מְדַבֵּר וְזֶה בָא וג׳|translate=he}} was ''yet speaking, and there came another'', &c.; see the numerous examples in {{GHGpar|111|g}} and {{GHGpar|116|u}}. Instead of a complete noun-clause there often occurs a simple ''casus pendens'' after {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} with a participial attribute in the sense of ''whenever any one''..., e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=זׄבֵחַ זֶ֫בַח וּבָא וג׳ כָּל־אִישׁ|translate=whenever any man offered sacrifice, then came}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=23}}, &c.; see the examples (in which the second member is generally introduced by {{GHGterm|wāw apodosis}}) in {{GHGpar|116|w}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|164|b}}
(''b'') Sequence is expressed by the juxtaposition

(''1'') of two imperfects consecutive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּכַל לְהַשְׁקֹתוֹ וַתֹּאמֶר|translate=and when she had done giving him drink, she said}}, &c.; 28:8 f., 29:31, 30:9, 32:26, &c.; cf. {{GHGpar|111|d}};

(2) of a noun-clause with a passive participle as predicate, and a verbal-clause attached by {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=25}}; cf. {{GHGpar|116|v}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=29}} an imperative follows without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}};

(3) of two perfects (frequently with the secondary idea of rapid succession<ref>This secondary idea is implied here by the mere co-ordination of two independent {{GHGterm|verbal}}-clauses, just as the idea of simultaneous occurrence (according to {{GHGpar|116|u}}, note 1) is implied in the co-ordination of a ''noun''-clause with another clause. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=30}} the immediate succession is especially emphasized by {{GHGheb|text=אַךְ}} and the infinitive absolute, ''Jacob was yet scarce gone out... then Esau his brother came''; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=24}} by {{GHGheb|text=אַךְ}} only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=48|verse=6}} by {{GHGheb|text=כֵּן}} and the addition of two more perfects without {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}.</ref> of the two actions or events in past time), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=הַשֶּׁ֫מָשׁ יָצָא... וְלוֹט בָּא וג׳|translate=the sun was just risen..., and}} (=when) ''Lot came'', &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=24}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=3}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=39|hidebook=1}} f.—In all these examples the subject follows immediately after the connective {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, and then the (simple) perfect. On the other hand,

(4) a perfect consecutive follows another perfect consecutive to express the contingent succession of future actions, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהִשַּׂגְתָּם וְאָֽטַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם}}<section end=par164 /><noinclude>
